subject: Production: AtlasAI semantic-index p95/p99 regression after catalog promotion
messages:
From: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@atlasai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T08:14:21-07:00
Subject: Spike in p95/p99 for semantic-index endpoint after catalog promotion (URGENT)

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a significant latency regression on our semantic-index (vectors) calls shortly after your catalog promotion rolled out to hosted. p95 has jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms and p99 is above 2s. This started at ~07:50 PT and has been intermittent but frequent. Our production job that batches 600 requests/min is timing out on retry and that’s causing downstream backpressure.

I attached a short PNG showing p95/p99 from New Relic and a trace dump from one of our failing requests. Can you confirm whether AtlasAI was included in the catalog promotion at ~07:30? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is customer-impacting for our search product.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Parker
Head of Platform Engineering, AtlasAI
ellen.parker@atlasai.com

Attachments: latency_trend_may12.png, trace_dump_region-west-20280512.zip

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@atlasai.com>, Atlas AI Infra <infra@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T08:25:03-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 for semantic-index endpoint after catalog promotion (URGENT)

Ellen — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I’m escalating immediately.

Quick answers: yes, a catalog promotion targeting the semantics-index family completed at 07:28 PT (we promoted a quantized variant and adjusted kernel pins in west region). We’re standing up an incident bridge now and I’ve looped in SRE and the model-onboarding owners (Marissa, Neha). I’ll share a short mitigation plan within 15 minutes.

I know this is customer-critical — we’ll prioritize AtlasAI.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T08:29:44-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 for semantic-index endpoint after catalog promotion (URGENT)

Adding quick findings from the runtime side (hit cache):
- Promotion included a new quantized variant (q3) for the semantic-index model family and a kernel swap for AMD instances in us-west-2.
- Early telemetry shows increased tokenization latency for some long inputs (Atlas has variable-length vectors). That looks like an unexpected slowpath in the tokenizer->KV cache warmup.
- Batching behavior changed slightly after kernel swap; effective batch packing for Atlas traffic dropped, increasing per-request overhead.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Roll back this promotion for AtlasAI only (can pin them to previous model variant within 10 minutes).
2) Temporarily route AtlasAI to capacity pool with older kernel pins (we can spin up a fallback pool in us-west-2, ~12-18m).
3) Enable a per-account TTL bypass for KV cache to force local warm caches for Atlas traffic (risk: short-term higher memory).

I recommend option (1) + (3) to reduce latency quickly. I’ll prepare a rollback job and test it in canary for a single customer allocation.

Marissa
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Model Onboarding

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T08:42:12-07:00
Subject: Action plan: rollback + cache TTL for AtlasAI (ETA ~20m)

Ellen — we have a targeted mitigation plan and a timeline: 
- 08:40 PT: Prepare rollback package to pin AtlasAI to the pre-promotion model variant.
- 08:50 PT: Execute canary rollback for a single allocation and monitor p95/p99 for 10 minutes.
- 09:05 PT: If metrics recover, roll AtlasAI fully back to previous variant (expected within 10–12 minutes).
- In parallel, we will enable a short-lived per-account KV cache TTL bypass to force warm caches for Atlas traffic (6–8 min effect).

We will provide continuous updates on the bridge. If anything changes I’ll escalate to the ops execs. We can also offer a compensation credit for the incident — I’ll coordinate with finance and your account team.

Do you want us to proceed with rollback now?

— Logan

From: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@atlasai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas AI Infra <infra@atlasai.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T08:46:55-07:00
Subject: Re: Action plan: rollback + cache TTL for AtlasAI (ETA ~20m)

Please proceed with the rollback and TTL bypass immediately. We’re seeing user-facing timeouts on search and need mitigation now. We prefer rollback + TTL bypass as you suggested. Keep me posted on the 10-minute canary results.

Ellen

Date: 2028-05-12T09:12:09-07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation update: metrics recovered, recommend follow-up changes

Summary: rollback + TTL bypass executed 08:52–09:03 PT (canary -> full). Observed effects: p95 for AtlasAI semantic-index dropped from ~850ms to ~110ms within 3 minutes of full rollback. p99 dropped below 400ms.

Actions completed:
- Rolled AtlasAI to previous pre-promotion variant (rollback id: RB-20280512-01).
- Enabled per-account KV cache TTL bypass for Atlas (6 minutes) to accelerate cache warming.
- Temporarily increased dedicated pool capacity for Atlas allocations by 20% while we investigate root cause.

Next steps (post-incident):
- Marissa to run a regression test on variable-length inputs and tokenizer slowpath (owner).
- Aditya to produce a short postmortem draft with timeline and recommended catalog gating criteria (owner).
- Hannah to coordinate exec brief and credit offer with Sales Ops (owner).

Customer outcome: Ellen confirms recovery and asked for a follow-up call later today to review permanent mitigations and compensation.

Neha
SRE, Redwood Inference
